title: The two bypass history rows carry their predecessor's standing
intention: The two class-space history rows that lack `standing` because CC bypassed the projector on 2026-10-02 — cairn/devices/tester/history.json seq 64 and cairn/machines/counting_block/history.json seq 2 — carry their predecessor row's standing ('BUILDME' in both), written through the artifact door, while diagnostic_inspector seq 4 is left as written (Akien: "i, leave the july one").
why: Child B of 471aa05ba639. tester history seq 64 and counting_block history seq 2 were appended by CC on 2026-10-02 through artifact.write verb append, past projector.append_entry's floor, so they lack `standing`; test_every_real_history_on_disk_would_pass_the_gate is red naming them beside the kept exhibit diagnostic_inspector seq 4. 62a57b781efc closed the door; these two rows are what passed before it closed. Akien chose the repair set and rule ("i, leave the july one" — relayed by peer akiendelllinux_cc_0, message 8o; recorded as open-a13486d0510d).
traces_to: Law 7 (a history row is a record of truth and the floor reads it); Law 4 (62a57b781efc closed the door; this repairs what passed before it closed); the parent 471aa05ba639's falsifier.
how: One script loads each history.json, sets standing on the one named row to the standing of the row before it (seq 63 / seq 1, both 'BUILDME', measured 2026-10-06), and writes the whole body back through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(abs path, verb='write', why=<Akien's answer, cites 8o>). The door journals it (history_integrity accepts it once committed) and 62a57b781efc's floor passes it because the changed row now carries standing. No `repair` verb exists in VERBS (artifact.py:64); `cairn artifact hand-edit` parks for Akien's approval, which spends his bandwidth on a change the door itself can carry. Measure: cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_append_door_instrument.py, unchanged — its tooth test_every_real_history_on_disk_would_pass_the_gate is red at HEAD 3a11b2aa naming exactly the three rows, and asserts the only offender is diagnostic_inspector seq 4. Proof of this ticket's own: cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_the_two_bypass_rows_carry_their_predecessors_standing.py (written red-first, one composite tooth for the falsifier's one clause, PROVES['ba8c62b8203e']['all']) — added because the chart's validate judge needs a proof declaring PROVES for this ticket and cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_append_door_instrument.py stays as written; cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_append_door_instrument.py is run beside it.
falsifier: Done when cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_the_two_bypass_rows_carry_their_predecessors_standing.py is green (each of the two rows carries a non-empty standing equal to its predecessor's, and diagnostic_inspector seq 4 still lacks it) and cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_append_door_instrument.py runs 12/12 green, both under bin/cairn test, with cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_append_door_instrument.py byte-identical to HEAD 3a11b2aa (its tooth test_every_real_history_on_disk_would_pass_the_gate is red there now naming exactly tester 64, counting_block 2, diagnostic_inspector 4); each history's only change is that one added key (json-equal otherwise), with two journal entries in .artifact-journal.jsonl. Horizon: this voyage. Wrong intent if a predecessor's standing is not the row's true standing — both rows were appended by their voyage (06f0445e7a63, 5a4ec289bf15) directly after its BUILDME crossing and before any other crossing, so BUILDME is the state they stood in.
watchme: none, because the tooth test_every_real_history_on_disk_would_pass_the_gate in cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_append_door_instrument.py re-reads every class-space history on each run, and 62a57b781efc (PROVED) refuses a new row without standing at the artifact door, so a recurrence reds there with no probe to build
children: none, because the repair is two field writes through one door, measured by one existing proof (cairn/tools/charter/proofs/test_append_door_instrument.py)
